# onetsolutions_instance_gpu (Resource)

Attaches a GPU to an instance, billed by the hour while it stays attached.

~> **Billing.** A GPU is **billed by the hour** (`hourly_rate`) from the moment it is attached
until it is detached; `billed_minutes` shows the use billed so far. `terraform plan` shows the
hourly rate of the GPU it attaches as a warning. Destroying the resource detaches the GPU, which
ends its billing.

!> **Attaching and detaching restart the instance.** Each operation stops the instance, changes its
hardware and starts it again, so plan them outside busy hours. The instance is left **running**,
even one that was stopped: an `onetsolutions_instance` with `state = "stopped"` is stopped again
by its next apply. Changing `model` or `instance_id` detaches the GPU and attaches a new one: two
restarts. `deletion_protection = true` refuses a destroy or a replacement, so the GPU is not
released by mistake: another instance on the same server may take it.

An instance holds one GPU at most. The models that can be attached depend on the server hosting the
instance: list them with `onetsolutions_instance_available_gpus`. A model that is not available is
refused at plan time. While another operation runs on the instance, the attachment waits for it to
end, up to the timeout. A GPU detached in the console, or an instance that no longer exists,
removes the resource from the state at the next refresh.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_instance_available_gpus" "web" {
  instance_id = onetsolutions_instance.web.id
}

# Billed by the hour while attached. Attaching and detaching stop and start the instance.
resource "onetsolutions_instance_gpu" "inference" {
  instance_id = onetsolutions_instance.web.id
  model       = "NVIDIA L4"

  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = contains(data.onetsolutions_instance_available_gpus.web.gpus[*].model, "NVIDIA L4")
      error_message = "No NVIDIA L4 is free on the host of this instance."
    }
  }
}

output "gpu_hourly_rate" {
  value = onetsolutions_instance_gpu.inference.hourly_rate
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The UUID of the instance the GPU is attached to. Changing it detaches the GPU and attaches one to the new instance.
- `model` (String) The GPU model to attach, as `onetsolutions_instance_available_gpus` lists it for the instance, such as `NVIDIA L4`. Changing it detaches the GPU and attaches one of the new model.

### Optional

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether destroying (or replacing) the attachment is refused, so the GPU is not released by mistake. Defaults to `false`.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `attached_at` (String) When the GPU was attached and its billing started (RFC 3339).
- `billed_minutes` (Number) The minutes of use billed so far for this attachment, as of the last refresh.
- `hourly_rate` (String) The price of an hour of the GPU, as a decimal string.
- `id` (String) The UUID of the GPU attachment.
- `status` (String) The status of the attachment: `pending`, `active` or `detaching`.
- `vendor` (String) The vendor of the GPU, such as `nvidia`.
- `vram_gb` (Number) The memory of the GPU in GB, null when unknown.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the creation, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `20m`.
- `delete` (String) How long to wait for the deletion, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `20m`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_instance_gpu.inference
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/4c5d6e7f-8a9b-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<instance_id>/<attachment_id>, or <instance_id>/<attachment_id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_instance_gpu.inference 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/4c5d6e7f-8a9b-4c0d-9e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f
```
